title: Physiological extra-uterine support through extreme prematurity

concept.text: The proposed innovation is temporary physiological support that allows an extremely premature infant to continue developing after delivery through a period ordinarily spent in the uterus. An artificial-placenta system would need to sustain gas exchange and circulation, provide nutrition and temperature regulation, and maintain a protected developmental environment while the infant’s organs mature. The objective is a coordinated developmental support system, rather than the achievement of any one support function in isolation. This is a synthesis of the supplied concept; the retained source content does not independently establish these requirements.

The scope begins after extremely premature delivery and ends with a safe transition to an appropriate form of subsequent care. It does not require development outside the uterus from conception. Success would therefore mean bridging a vulnerable developmental interval while preserving the infant’s capacity to mature, with safe entry onto and exit from the system treated as part of the capability.

significance.text: If safe and effective, this capability could change care at gestational ages where survival is uncertain and immature organs constrain treatment. Its potentially revolutionary contribution would be to sustain development while reducing dependence on organs that are not yet ready to perform their usual functions after birth. That physiological achievement would be valuable only insofar as it translated into better outcomes for infants; maintaining circulation or gas exchange alone would not establish clinical benefit. This is a conditional assessment of the proposed innovation.

The direct hoped-for consequences are improved survival and better long-term developmental outcomes compared with the best available conventional care. Conditional downstream possibilities include reducing complications associated with extreme prematurity and changing which infants can benefit from sustained developmental support. Those possibilities depend on the balance of benefits and harms, the gestational ages and clinical circumstances in which the system works, and whether it can be delivered reliably in practice.

The artificial-placenta analogy describes the intended support role; it should not be read as proof that a device reproduces every function of the placenta or uterus. Likewise, temporary support after delivery would not demonstrate complete external gestation or eliminate the consequences of prematurity. The scale of the advance would be determined by demonstrated clinical outcomes and the boundaries of safe use, rather than by resemblance to a uterine environment.

missing_breakthrough.text: The unsolved capability is an integrated system that can sustain development through extreme prematurity without introducing harms that offset its benefits. As a proposed engineering formulation, this requires gas exchange, circulation, nutrition, temperature regulation and environmental protection to work together over the necessary developmental interval. Providing these functions individually would not establish that their combined operation supports healthy maturation.

The candidate identifies infection, clotting, brain injury and injury during transfer onto or off the system as central hazards. These make the challenge more demanding than simply extending the duration of extracorporeal support: sustained physiological stability, compatibility between blood and device materials, protection from contamination, and safe transitions must all be achieved together. This barrier analysis is a synthesis of the supplied problem statement, not a source-verified list of requirements or demonstrated failure modes.

A further translational barrier is establishing when physiological support actually improves human development. An animal system may provide useful evidence about feasibility, yet differences in developmental stage and clinical circumstances limit what can be inferred about infants. The necessary breakthrough therefore includes both dependable engineering and evidence identifying a human treatment window in which the overall balance of benefit and harm is favorable.

current_state.text: The supplied research attributes to Emily A. Partridge and colleagues a report dated 25 April 2017, titled “An extra-uterine system to physiologically support the extreme premature lamb,” with DOI 10.1038/ncomms15112. It describes support of developmentally premature lambs for up to four weeks, with reported growth and organ-development observations, including lung and brain maturation. These are attributed historical findings: their duration, methods and developmental outcomes could not be verified from the scientific content available to the supplied review.

The access limitation materially constrains interpretation. According to the supplied review, the retained PubMed artifact contains only a cookie-access notice, with no abstract, methods, results or figures. Although the source index records a saved artifact, successful saving does not establish that scientific content was captured. The review could not verify the study’s identity from that content. The earlier assertions that an abstract had been inspected and that a publisher page had failed to open are not substantiated by the retained material.

The reported 2017 animal result should therefore remain visible with this qualification, rather than be treated as disproved by an access failure. Even if verified, animal growth and maturation observations would not by themselves establish human safety, improved survival or comparative long-term developmental benefit. No freshness search record was supplied to assess subsequent progress through 1 November 2026, so these inputs do not establish the present clinical state or whether later work has resolved any of those questions.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: show that an integrated system can sustain the intended physiological functions throughout a clinically relevant developmental interval, with documented growth and organ maturation, acceptable complications, and safe transfer onto and off support. Evaluation should examine infection, clotting and neurological injury alongside physiological performance. These are proposed criteria for convincing evidence, not established consensus standards; the supplied material does not justify a particular duration or numerical safety threshold.
completion_criteria.label: Integrated support safely sustains physiological functions, growth and organ maturation

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical criterion: comparative studies should demonstrate improved survival and long-term developmental outcomes against the best available conventional care. Survival alone would not satisfy the supplied objective. Studies should identify which gestational ages and clinical circumstances benefit, how uncertainty affects treatment selection, and whether harms emerge after the support period. The choice of comparator, developmental measures and follow-up duration would need explicit justification.
completion_criteria.label: Improved survival and long-term development versus best available conventional care

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical criterion: results should be reproducible across independent teams and relevant care settings, with clearly described operating requirements, transfer procedures and limits of use. Evidence should establish how reliably the system can be used under the circumstances for which benefit is claimed. Finite studies would demonstrate effectiveness across the populations and conditions tested; they would not establish universal suitability for all premature infants.
completion_criteria.label: Independent teams reproduce results across relevant care settings

related_concepts.text: Conceptual relationship to BME-13, “Durable autonomous artificial-organ replacement”: both involve engineered support for physiological functions. BME-09 concerns a temporary bridge during development, with the infant’s own organs expected to mature sufficiently for transition off the system. BME-13 concerns durable replacement of organ function. Demonstrating temporary developmental support would not establish durable autonomous replacement.

Conceptual relationship to BME-16, “Long-lived tissue-integrated interfaces for implants,” and BME-14, “Shelf-stable, broadly compatible replacement for critical blood functions”: these concepts overlap with questions of biological compatibility, interfaces and the maintenance of critical physiological functions. BME-09 remains a coordinated developmental support system. Neither a successful implant interface nor a replacement for selected blood functions would independently supply its full capability.

Conceptual relationship to BME-01, “Manufacturing transplantable human organs on demand,” BME-11, “Controlled regeneration of complex organs in the adult body,” and BME-12, “Reliable, scalable animal-to-human organ transplantation”: all address limitations of organ function, but through different mechanisms. BME-09 aims to support the maturation of an infant’s existing organs. It does not require manufacturing, regenerating or transplanting replacement organs, and animal support experiments are distinct from animal-to-human organ transplantation.

Conceptual relationship to BME-10, “Validated patient-specific models for testing treatments before use,” and BME-18, “Long-lived continuous sensing of multiple clinically useful biomarkers”: modeling and sensing could potentially help select patients or monitor developmental support. These are possible enabling relationships inferred from the roster titles, not demonstrated dependencies in the supplied evidence. Predictions or monitoring measurements would still require validation against meaningful physiological and clinical outcomes.

brief.title: More time for very premature babies to develop
possible: Babies born far too early could keep developing outside the womb before moving to other care. A temporary support system would supply oxygen and nutrients, maintain blood flow and warmth, and provide a protected environment while their organs mature.
why: For families facing extreme prematurity, the goal is better survival and healthier development over the long term. Supporting babies without making their immature lungs take over breathing could reduce complications while giving those organs time to grow.

sources.showed: They supported premature lambs using an oxygen-supplying device connected through the umbilical cord and a closed fluid environment. They reported stable circulation, growth, and lung and brain maturation.
sources.quote: We show that fetal lambs that are developmentally equivalent to the extreme premature human infant can be physiologically supported in this extra-uterine device for up to 4 weeks.
sources.cited_for: The study supports the feasibility of sustaining development outside the womb in premature lambs.
sources.not_established: Lamb development does not establish safe treatment or better long-term outcomes for human infants.

sources.showed: In a small study, the team supported extremely premature lambs for up to two weeks. They maintained circulation, but body and organ growth were abnormal.
sources.quote: Fetal systemic circulation was maintained without infection, but growth was abnormal.
sources.cited_for: The study shows that maintaining circulation does not necessarily preserve healthy growth.
sources.not_established: The system has yet to demonstrate healthy growth alongside stable circulation in these extremely premature animals.

sources.showed: Supported lambs had brain tissue and patterns of gene activity resembling those of lambs that continued developing in the womb to a comparable age.
sources.quote: There were no clinically relevant histological differences between the control late pre-term and EXTEND ovine brain tissues.
sources.cited_for: The study supports continued brain maturation during support outside the womb.
sources.not_established: Similar brain tissue and gene activity do not establish normal long-term brain function or benefit in human infants.

shown: Partridge and colleagues sustained premature lambs outside the womb for up to four weeks, with growth and organ maturation. Animal studies have demonstrated parts of the capability; improved survival and long-term development in human infants remain to be shown.
missing: An integrated system must sustain healthy maturation while supplying oxygen, circulation, nutrition, warmth and protection.
Transfers onto and off support must be safe, with infection, blood clots and brain injury kept at acceptable levels.
Comparative human studies must demonstrate better survival and long-term development than the best conventional care.
Independent teams must reproduce the benefits across relevant care settings.

milestones.label: Safe support sustains growth and organ maturation
milestones.explanation: A complete system would have to sustain body functions, growth and organ maturation, with acceptable complications and safe transfers. This would establish that it supports development throughout the vulnerable period.

milestones.label: Infants survive and develop better than with conventional care
milestones.explanation: Comparative studies would have to show better survival and long-term development than the best conventional care. This would establish a benefit for infants beyond keeping their bodies functioning during support.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce benefits across care settings
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce results across relevant care settings, with clear procedures and limits of use. This would establish how reliably the treatment works in practice.

uncertain: Which ages at birth and clinical circumstances offer infants the best balance of benefit and harm?
How long must support last, and what complication rates would be acceptable?
Which developmental measures and length of follow-up would establish a lasting benefit?

page.title: Artificial-womb support for extremely premature infants
page.definition: A temporary system supports an infant born before 28 completed weeks of gestation in a fluid environment, supplying gas exchange outside the body while preserving fetal circulation and allowing organs to mature. The infant subsequently transitions to neonatal care.

goal.need: In FDA's presentation of United States 2021 vital statistics, infants born before 28 weeks accounted for 0.6% of live births and 40% of infant deaths. Artificial-womb development targets this group by supporting organ maturation while deferring pulmonary gas exchange.

figures.caption: United States births and infant deaths associated with birth before 28 weeks, 2021
rows: Deaths of infants born before 28 weeks
figures.note: The percentages have different denominators. Figures are those presented by FDA.

statements.quote: provide a bridge from extreme preterm birth to later gestation within a physiologic environment aimed at mimicking the womb.
statements.context: The passage describes the intended function of artificial-womb devices for extremely premature infants.

statements.body: Perinatal Life Support consortium, European Commission Horizon 2020 project
statements.quote: support the safe development of EP infants outside the womb by preserving the innate fetal cardiorespiratory physiology ex vivo
statements.context: EP means extremely preterm; ex vivo means outside the body. The project began on 1 October 2019.

statements.body: Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, Center for Fetal Research
statements.quote: This technology is designed to maintain normal fetal physiology and development by mimicking, as closely as possible, the environment of the maternal womb

completion.title: An artificial-womb device receives FDA premarket approval for supporting extremely premature infants.
completion.criterion: FDA issues a premarket approval (PMA) order for an artificial-womb device indicated to bridge extremely premature infants from delivery to later maturation and subsequent neonatal care. The evidence establishes reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness for the labelled population and conditions of use, and the application satisfies manufacturing and other approval requirements.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Class III device marketing requirements and PMA approval-order guidance.
completion.threshold_quote: Before the FDA approves a PMA, the sponsor must provide valid scientific evidence demonstrating reasonable assurances of safety and effectiveness for the device’s intended use.
completion.basis: FDA identifies artificial-womb technologies as Class III significant-risk devices; its Class III pathway requires PMA supported by valid scientific evidence. Approval for the bridging indication tests an integrated human treatment. Vitara describes its system as investigational and reports no marketing authorization.

milestones.title: A preterm animal on artificial-womb support maintains organ perfusion and oxygenation.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate extracorporeal blood flow sufficient for organ perfusion and oxygenation in a preterm animal. Partridge and colleagues, published on 25 April 2017, supported eight lambs through umbilical vessels: five entered at 105–108 gestational days and received 25–28 days of support; three entered at 115–120 days and received 20–28 days. They reported fetal circulation and oxygenation. The 28-day maximum reflected an animal-protocol limit.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, briefing for the Pediatric Advisory Committee on 19 September 2023, section 3.3.1; a recommended physiological proof-of-concept criterion.
milestones.threshold_quote: adequate extracorporeal circuit flow to support end organ perfusion and oxygenation.

milestones.title: Artificial-womb support preserves animal organ development and improves lung development over ventilation.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate gestational-age-appropriate organ growth, maturation and protection from injury in developmentally relevant models, with lung development improved over mechanical-ventilation controls. On 24 August 2023, Usuda and colleagues reported six lambs supported from 95 gestational days for up to 336 hours versus six in-utero controls; several organ weights were reduced. On 21 November 2024, Cohen and colleagues reported brain histology without clinically relevant differences between five supported lambs examined at 125–128 gestational days and two late-preterm controls; two earlier-preterm controls were also studied. These findings address parts of the criterion.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, briefing for the Pediatric Advisory Committee on 19 September 2023, section 3.3.1; recommended nonclinical evidence of growth, maturation and protection across organ systems.
milestones.threshold_quote: Normal growth and protection from injury should be demonstrated across organ systems

milestones.title: The first extremely premature infant receives artificial-womb support in an authorized human study.
milestones.criterion: Treat the first human infant for the proposed indication after FDA investigational device exemption (IDE) and institutional review board (IRB) approval. FDA also requires that anticipated benefit justify risk and that the benefit–risk relation be at least as favorable as available alternatives under 21 CFR 50.52. This milestone is actual treatment under an authorized protocol.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, artificial-womb regulatory presentation on 19 September 2023, pediatric safeguards, and its published definition of a first-in-human study.
milestones.threshold_quote: IDE and IRB approval required before initiating enrollment

milestones.title: An early feasibility study demonstrates artificial-womb function and initial clinical safety in infants.
milestones.criterion: An IDE early feasibility study provides proof of principle and initial clinical safety data for artificial-womb support in the intended infant population. FDA describes these studies as generally involving fewer than 10 initial subjects; this is a study-size convention, not a minimum success count. Success is assessed against the authorized protocol's safety and device-function objectives.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, early feasibility study guidance, sections 3 and 11; the agency explicitly applies early feasibility principles to artificial-womb development in its 2023 briefing.
milestones.threshold_quote: Early feasibility studies may be used to provide proof of principle and initial clinical safety data.

milestones.title: A pivotal study supplies evidence of artificial-womb safety and effectiveness for its intended use.
milestones.criterion: A pivotal clinical investigation supplies valid scientific evidence sufficient for FDA to determine reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness in the intended infant population and conditions of use. The study evaluates clinically meaningful safety and effectiveness endpoints under its prespecified design. This milestone is the supporting clinical result; completion is the subsequent PMA approval order.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Design Considerations for Pivotal Clinical Investigations for Medical Devices, section 3.2; a general device evidentiary criterion, without an artificial-womb-specific numerical performance goal.
milestones.threshold_quote: The results of the study must provide sufficient evidence for FDA to make a determination of reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness

not_found: No universal numerical support duration, survival improvement or neurodevelopmental success threshold was identified in FDA's public artificial-womb documents.
Web searches, including ClinicalTrials.gov-targeted searches for artificial womb, artificial placenta and EXTEND, did not identify a public human treatment protocol or published human outcome report.

results.finding: Eight preterm lambs maintained placental-equivalent circuit flow on artificial-womb support for up to 28 days.
results.detail: The lambs had normal fetal oxygen delivery and maintained fetal circulation. The longest runs ended at the 28-day animal-protocol limit.
results.quote: We have run 8 lambs with maintenance of stable levels of circuit flow equivalent to the normal flow to the placenta.

results.finding: Eight umbilically supported lambs showed lung maturation in parallel with age-matched controls.
results.detail: The study reports growth and organ maturation, but does not demonstrate improved lung development over mechanical-ventilation controls.
results.quote: Morphometric analysis demonstrated progression from the canalicular to saccular stages of lung development in parallel with age-matched normal control lambs (

results.finding: Six preterm lambs maintained systemic circulation on artificial placenta support for a mean of 250 hours.
results.detail: Cord blood gases remained clinically acceptable. Five animals were euthanized before the planned 336-hour endpoint because of bleeding or umbilical artery vasoconstriction.
results.quote: Mean survival was 250 ± 72 h (Max 336 h) with systemic circulation and key physiological parameters maintained mostly within normal ranges.

results.finding: Six supported lambs had reduced lung, liver and kidney weights compared with in-utero controls.
results.detail: Growth was abnormal, and the study did not compare lung development with mechanically ventilated controls. The abstract reports six controls, while the methods and results tables report eight.
results.quote:
Fetal lung, liver, and kidney weights and humerus length gain in the APT Group were less than those of the
in-utero
Control Group.

results.finding: Five EXTEND-supported lambs had no clinically relevant brain histology differences from two late-preterm controls.
results.detail: The study assessed brain development, but did not establish appropriate growth and protection across organs or improved lung development versus mechanical ventilation. Each control cohort had two lambs.
results.quote: There were no clinically relevant histological differences between the control late pre-term and EXTEND ovine brain tissues.

results.finding: Five supported lambs had a lung development marker area fraction of 0.012, versus 0.003 in three early-ventilated controls.
results.detail: Supported lambs also had less lung injury than early-ventilated controls. The study focused on lungs and did not demonstrate gestational-age-appropriate growth and maturation across organs. The supported group was a selected cohort, and two early-control lungs were too injured for marker analysis.
results.quote: The area fraction of positive alveolar tips was significantly higher in AP lungs than both early MV and late MV lungs (0.012±0.003 vs. 0.003±0.0005; p=0.001 and 0.004±0.002; p=0.001;

results.finding: Six EXTEND-supported lambs showed progressive brain medullation, as did three gestationally matched controls.
results.detail: Brain assessments were qualitative and underpowered; four other lambs died before the study endpoint. The study did not compare lung development with mechanical ventilation.
results.quote: Microscopic analysis showed evidence of progressive medullation (axonal sheath development and myelination) of the radiating cerebrocortical white matter tracts in both study groups.

results.finding: In 17 preterm lambs supported for 2–4 weeks, ileal epithelial and enteric nervous system maturation appeared normal.
results.detail: Age-matched in-utero lambs served as controls. Peyer’s patch organization was impaired, and the study did not compare lung development with mechanical ventilation.
results.quote: EXTEND supports normal ileal epithelial and enteric nervous system maturation in pre-term lambs.

results.finding: Eight preterm lambs maintained circuit flow equivalent to normal placental flow for up to 28 days.
results.detail: The lambs maintained normal fetal oxygen delivery and fetal circulation. The longest runs ended at 28 days because of animal-protocol limitations.
results.quote: We have run 8 lambs with maintenance of stable levels of circuit flow equivalent to the normal flow to the placenta.

results.finding: Five supported lamb brains showed no evidence of haemorrhage or infarct on whole-brain sectioning.
results.detail: Lung development progressed in parallel with age-matched controls, but the study did not demonstrate improved lung development over mechanically ventilated preterm controls. Neurologic findings were qualified by model and follow-up limitations.
results.quote:
On whole-brain sectioning we observed no evidence of haemorrhage or infarct in any of the UA/UV animal brains (
n
=5).

results.finding: Ten extremely preterm lambs received EXTEND support for a mean of 13.5 days with stable hemodynamics and oxygenation.
results.detail: Four additional lambs died before reaching the study endpoint and were excluded from the study group.
results.quote: Hemodynamics and oxygenation showed stable parameters.

results.finding: Brain MRI and histology in 6 EXTEND-supported lambs were comparable to those in 3 gestationally equivalent controls.
results.detail: The study was underpowered to detect even major brain-development differences. It did not compare lung development with mechanically ventilated controls.
results.quote:
MRI volumetric and diffusion analysis was comparable to controls.
Histologic brain analysis revealed no difference between study groups.

results.finding: Sheep on liquid-incubator support survived for 21 days; sample size was not reported.
results.detail: The system uses extracorporeal circulation and an oxygenating membrane, but the report gives no measurements of blood flow, organ perfusion or oxygenation.
results.quote: Using a sheep model, the team has so far designed and described the surgical techniques and protocols required to carry out a transition from the uterus to a prototype liquid incubator without incident, and has achieved a survival rate of 21 days within the system.

results.finding: One supported lamb had normal long-term neurodevelopmental results after more than one year.
results.detail: The report does not establish gestational-age-appropriate organ growth and protection or improved lung development against mechanically ventilated controls.

results.finding: Twelve premature lambs maintained physiological circulation and oxygenation on EXTEND support for over 14 days.
results.detail: Six received systemic heparin and six did not. Fifteen of 27 enrolled animals died before 14 days and were excluded from the analysis.
results.quote: Both study groups demonstrated overall hemodynamic stability, with no significant differences in blood flow or blood flow per weight.
